subject: Climate & Environment
title: The IPCC and Global Consensus
description: A fast breakdown of The IPCC and Global Consensus for builders.

hook.text: In 1988, the United Nations created a panel to settle the climate debate with science.

buildup.text: The IPCC gathers thousands of scientists to review every climate study on the planet.

discovery.text: Their reports synthesize what the world already knows, not original research.

twist.text: Every sentence in the summary is approved word by word by government representatives.

climax.text: Despite that political filter, the IPCC's conclusion is blunt: humans cause warming.

punchline.text: Thousands of scientists, one conclusion: it's us.

details.summary: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change synthesizes climate research from thousands of scientists worldwide into comprehensive assessment reports. Its findings, approved line by line by governments, represent the strongest scientific consensus on any global issue.
details.whyItMatters: The IPCC is the global authority on climate science. Its reports directly shape international negotiations, national policies, and corporate strategies.
takeaways: The IPCC does not conduct research but reviews existing literature
Assessment reports involve thousands of scientists from 195 countries
Reports are approved line by line by government representatives

faq.question: How often does the IPCC publish assessment reports?
faq.answer: Major assessment reports appear roughly every six to seven years, with the Sixth Assessment completed in 2023. Special reports on specific topics like 1.5 degrees or oceans are published between cycles as needed.

faq.question: Why is the IPCC process considered conservative?
faq.answer: Government approval means every line must be accepted by all 195 member states, including major fossil fuel producers. This consensus requirement tends to produce cautious language and understate worst-case risks.
